steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for a computer vision paper presenting SAI3D, our zero-shot 3D instance segmentation method built on the Segment Anything Model. It should explain the limits of supervised methods and of recent foundation-model-based 3D approaches, describe our method and evaluation, and end with a contributions list.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
- 3D instance segmentation and the limits of supervised methods
- Vision-language foundation models for 3D scene understanding
- SAM-based 3D methods and their weaknesses
- Our approach: SAI3D
- Evaluation and results
- Contributions

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
- 3D instance segmentation and the limits of supervised methods
  - task: parse 3D scene into objects = binary foreground masks + semantic labels
  - great progress, but SOTA is supervised, relies on precise 3D annotations
  - confined to narrow object categories of specific datasets (ScanNet, KITTI)
  - constrains open-world use: embodied agents, autonomous driving
- Vision-language foundation models
  - methods based on CLIP: impressive open-set semantic reasoning
  - recent studies use them for 3D scene comprehension (OpenScene, LERF)
  - limits: predict heatmap, no distinction between objects with same semantics
  - rely on specific prompts, not available for all objects in a scene
- SAM-based 3D methods
  - SAM: cutting-edge fine-grained image segmentation in complex scenes
  - SA3D: NeRF trained on 2D images; manual prompts in a single view (rough points on target); object masks in 3D grid via cross-view self-prompting with SAM
  - SAM3D: SAM automatic mask generation -> dense instance masks -> projected into 3D scene by iterative merging
  - SAM3D masks more detailed than ScanNet ground truth
  - but susceptible to 2D mask errors: local adjacent frame merging, may overlook global consensus
- Our approach: SAI3D
  - question: better leverage geometric priors + multi-view consistency for fine-grained instance segmentation of intricate scenes
  - SAI3D (Segment Any Instance in 3D Scenes): SAM for zero-shot 3D instance segmentation, no training/finetuning with 3D annotations
  - scene -> geometric primitives; sparse affinity matrix of pairwise similarity scores from SAM 2D masks
  - progressive merging with region-growing algorithm + aggregation of votes from all valid images -> multi-view consistent result
- Evaluation
  - ScanNetV2, ScanNet200, Matterport3D, recent ScanNet++
  - ScanNet++: more detailed masks, rich semantics, realistic and challenging in-the-wild benchmark
  - class-agnostic: significantly beats SAM3D and open-vocabulary baselines
  - on ScanNet++: zero-shot beats fully-supervised Mask3D trained on ScanNet
- Contributions
  - SAI3D: efficient zero-shot method, geometric priors + semantic-aware image segmentation
  - aggregation of 2D masks into coherent, view-consistent 3D segmentations
  - 3D masks more accurate than previous approaches; opens unsupervised 3D learning

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
The goal of 3D instance segmentation is to take a 3D scene and split it into a set of objects, where each object is represented as a binary foreground mask with a semantic label. 3D instance segmentation has made a lot of progress, but the state-of-the-art methods are supervised and they depend heavily on precise 3D annotations. Because of this they are limited to a small set of object categories in specific datasets such as ScanNet or KITTI. This is a big constraint on using them in open-world scenarios like embodied agents and autonomous driving.

Methods built on vision-language foundation models like CLIP have shown impressive performance at open-set semantic reasoning. These approaches have led to recent studies that look at how foundation models can help with understanding 3D scenes, for example OpenScene and LERF. These approaches achieve open-world 3D grounding, but they usually predict a heatmap and do not tell apart different objects that have the same semantics. They also rely on specific prompts, and these prompts might not be available for every object in a 3D scene.

More recently, the Segment Anything Model (SAM) got cutting-edge results for fine-grained image segmentation in complex scenes. Building on this, SA3D uses a NeRF trained on a set of 2D images. With manual prompts in a single view (rough points that represent the target object), it generates object masks in a 3D grid through cross-view self-prompting, which incorporates the functionalities of SAM. SAM3D goes further and uses SAM for automatic mask generation, which partitions images into dense instance masks, and then it projects them into the 3D scene through an iterative merging process. SAM3D can generate more detailed masks than the ground-truth annotations in ScanNet. But it is susceptible to 2D mask errors because the merging is done locally on adjacent frames, which might overlook global consensus.

- Our approach: SAI3D
  - better leverage geometric priors + multi-view consistency for fine-grained instance segmentation
  - SAI3D (Segment Any Instance in 3D Scenes): uses SAM, zero-shot, no training/finetuning with 3D annotations
  - geometric primitives; sparse affinity matrix from SAM 2D masks
  - region-growing merging + vote aggregation over all valid images -> multi-view consistent
- Evaluation
  - ScanNetV2, ScanNet200, Matterport3D, ScanNet++ (detailed masks, rich semantics, challenging)
  - class-agnostic: significantly beats SAM3D and open-vocabulary baselines
  - ScanNet++: zero-shot beats fully-supervised Mask3D trained on ScanNet
- Contributions
  - SAI3D method; view-consistent aggregation of 2D masks; more accurate 3D masks

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
The goal of 3D instance segmentation is to take a 3D scene and split it into a set of objects, where each object is represented as a binary foreground mask with a semantic label. 3D instance segmentation has made a lot of progress, but the state-of-the-art methods are supervised and they depend heavily on precise 3D annotations. Because of this they are limited to a small set of object categories in specific datasets such as ScanNet or KITTI. This is a big constraint on using them in open-world scenarios like embodied agents and autonomous driving.

Methods built on vision-language foundation models like CLIP have shown impressive performance at open-set semantic reasoning. These approaches have led to recent studies that look at how foundation models can help with understanding 3D scenes, for example OpenScene and LERF. These approaches achieve open-world 3D grounding, but they usually predict a heatmap and do not tell apart different objects that have the same semantics. They also rely on specific prompts, and these prompts might not be available for every object in a 3D scene.

More recently, the Segment Anything Model (SAM) got cutting-edge results for fine-grained image segmentation in complex scenes. Building on this, SA3D uses a NeRF trained on a set of 2D images. With manual prompts in a single view (rough points that represent the target object), it generates object masks in a 3D grid through cross-view self-prompting, which incorporates the functionalities of SAM. SAM3D goes further and uses SAM for automatic mask generation, which partitions images into dense instance masks, and then it projects them into the 3D scene through an iterative merging process. SAM3D can generate more detailed masks than the ground-truth annotations in ScanNet. But it is susceptible to 2D mask errors because the merging is done locally on adjacent frames, which might overlook global consensus.

In this work we look at how to make better use of geometric priors and multi-view consistency for fine-grained instance segmentation of intricate 3D scenes. We introduce SAI3D (Segment Any Instance in 3D Scenes). It uses SAM to do zero-shot 3D instance segmentation, with no training or finetuning on 3D annotations. SAI3D breaks the 3D scene into geometric primitives and builds a sparse affinity matrix with pairwise similarity scores based on the 2D masks that SAM generates. Then the primitives are merged progressively with a region-growing algorithm, and votes from all valid images are aggregated, so that we get a 3D instance segmentation that is consistent across multiple views.

We evaluate our method on ScanNetV2, ScanNet200, Matterport3D and also the recently developed ScanNet++. ScanNet++ has more detailed segmentation masks with rich semantics, so it is a more realistic and challenging benchmark for in-the-wild scenarios. For class-agnostic segmentation our method outperforms SAM3D and other open-vocabulary segmentation baselines by a large margin on both datasets. When evaluated on ScanNet++, our zero-shot method even gets better results than fully-supervised Mask3D models trained on ScanNet, which shows that SAI3D works well for fine-grained instance segmentation of complex 3D scenes.

Our contributions are:

- We introduce SAI3D, an efficient zero-shot 3D instance segmentation method that combines geometric priors and semantic-aware image segmentation.

- We present an aggregation method that turns 2D image masks into coherent 3D segmentations that are consistent across different views.

- We show that the generated 3D masks are more accurate than previous approaches, which opens new opportunities for unsupervised 3D learning.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
3D instance segmentation aims to parse a 3D scene into a set of objects represented as binary foreground masks with associated semantic labels. Although 3D instance segmentation has made great progress, state-of-the-art methods are supervised and rely heavily on precise 3D annotations. As a result, these methods are confined to a narrow scope of object categories within specific datasets like ScanNet [1] or KITTI [2], which considerably constrains their applications in open-world scenarios such as embodied agents and autonomous driving.

Advanced methods based on vision-language foundation models like CLIP [3] have shown impressive performance in open-set semantic reasoning. These approaches have prompted recent studies exploring how foundation models can assist in comprehending 3D scenes (e.g., OpenScene [4] and LERF [5]).

Although they achieve open-world 3D grounding, these approaches typically predict a heatmap without distinguishing among different objects with the same semantics. Moreover, they rely on specific prompts that might not be available for all objects within a 3D scene.

More recently, the Segment Anything Model (SAM) [6] has achieved cutting-edge results in fine-grained image segmentation within complex scenes. Building on this progress, SA3D [7] utilizes a NeRF trained on a set of 2D images. Using manual prompts in a single view (rough points representing the target object), it generates object masks within a 3D grid via cross-view self-prompting, incorporating the functionalities of SAM. Going further, SAM3D [8] employs SAM for automatic mask generation, partitioning images into dense instance masks and then projecting them into the 3D scene through an iterative merging process. Notably, SAM3D can generate more detailed masks than the ground-truth annotations in ScanNet. However, it is susceptible to 2D mask errors due to its local adjacent frame merging process, which might overlook global consensus.

In this work, we investigate how to better leverage geometric priors and multi-view consistency for fine-grained instance segmentation of intricate 3D scenes. We introduce SAI3D (Segment Any Instance in 3D Scenes), which takes advantage of SAM to perform zero-shot 3D instance segmentation without training or finetuning with 3D annotations. SAI3D dissects the 3D scene into geometric primitives and builds a sparse affinity matrix capturing pairwise similarity scores based on the 2D masks generated by SAM. Our approach progressively merges these primitives using a region-growing algorithm and aggregates votes from all valid images to obtain a multi-view consistent 3D instance segmentation.

We evaluate our method on ScanNetV2 [1], ScanNet200 [9], Matterport3D [10] and the recently developed ScanNet++ [11]. Notably, ScanNet++ provides more detailed segmentation masks with rich semantics, offering a more realistic and challenging benchmark for in-the-wild scenarios. For class-agnostic segmentation, our method significantly outperforms SAM3D and other open-vocabulary segmentation baselines on both datasets. Remarkably, on ScanNet++ our zero-shot method achieves better results than fully-supervised Mask3D models trained on ScanNet, underlining the efficacy of SAI3D for fine-grained instance segmentation of complex 3D scenes.

Overall, our contributions are summarized as follows:

- We introduce SAI3D, an efficient zero-shot 3D instance segmentation method that combines geometric priors and semantic-aware image segmentation.

- We present a carefully designed method for aggregating 2D image masks into coherent 3D segmentations that are consistent across views.

- We demonstrate that the generated 3D masks are more accurate than those of previous approaches, opening new opportunities for unsupervised 3D learning.
